transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, my doctor wanted me to come in because she says I’ve gotten too thin. I’ve noticed it too—my work pants are hanging loose on me now. But… I don’t know, part of me still feels kind of relieved when the number on the scale goes down.
Have you been worried about gaining weight or feeling like you might gain weight, even though you’ve already lost some?

Yes. I do worry about it. If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, then the rest of the day I’m scared it’s going to show on me somehow. I keep checking myself and thinking I need to make up for it.
After eating, do you ever make yourself sick or use laxatives to try to control your weight?
I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t make myself throw up, and I don’t take laxatives for that. I mostly just get anxious about what I ate.
Do you ever exercise a lot or restrict what you eat to make up for the food you’ve eaten and avoid gaining weight?

Yes, I do restrict what I eat. I’ll make a full plate for my husband and my mother-in-law, but when it’s time for me to eat, I usually talk myself into just having coffee, or some vegetables, or maybe half a piece of toast. It feels like that should be enough for me.
Do you find yourself avoiding eating certain foods or eating less overall because you’re afraid it will cause you to gain weight, even if others might encourage you to eat more?

Yes. I do eat less because I’m afraid of gaining weight. I’ll cook proper plates for my husband and my mother-in-law, but when I sit down for myself, I usually talk myself into just coffee, or a few vegetables, or maybe half a piece of toast. I tell myself that’s enough for me, even if they think I should eat more.
Have you ever felt that your weight is much lower than it should be, or have you been told that you are underweight?
Yes. My doctor has said I’ve gotten too thin. I notice it too, like my work pants hang really loose on me now. But… honestly, part of me still feels relieved when the number on the scale is lower.
Do you feel that your overall sense of who you are or how you feel about yourself is strongly influenced by your weight or body shape?

Yes. I think it does. When I feel small and neat, I feel like I’m keeping myself together, like I’m doing things right. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even a little full, I feel like I’ve let myself go.
